messages:
kevin: Quick sync - we need a small, auditable checklist that proves isolation for private installs. Customers want a tamper-evident chain: signed audit batches, netpol enforced egress to a KMS gateway, and minimal provisioning RBAC. Thoughts?

maya: Love the checklist idea. Two immediate asks: 1) image CVE gate (fail build if known high/critical CVE), 2) evidence bundle format (what do we include so an auditor can verify?).

lucas: For bundles: include signed digest of the audit log batch, netpol snapshot (kubectl get netpol -o yaml), ClusterRole/Binding manifests, and a signed marker from the wrapping key. Verify process: take SHA256 of artifacts -> sign with HSM key -> store signature + artifacts in immutable storage.

kevin: Good. Proposed artifact list: [sbom.json, image-cve-report.json, netpol.yaml, clusterrole-provisioner-limited.yaml, auditbatch.ndjson, signature.txt]. We should timestamp the signature using NTP-signed time or an internal timestamping service.

maya: About RBAC: instead of editing the live clusterrole, create a new role 'provisioner-limited' and bind it to the provisioner SA only in the canary namespace. That keeps rollbacks trivial. Example minimal role snippet I will add to the runbook: 
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: provisioner-limited
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
```

lucas: Netpol pattern: default-deny egress then allow to kms-gateway + monitoring IPs. Example for airgapped site (service-only): 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-kms-gw-only
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-gateway
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

kevin: How do we handle customer-managed KMS vs local HSM connectors? Policy-wise: require mTLS and an allowlist entry for customer KMS host; for local HSM, require connector bind to localhost and prohibit outbound. Document both as accepted modes with clear acceptance criteria.

maya: We should also add an automated verifier: post-rollout job that fetches the artifact bundle, verifies signatures, checks netpols are in place, and runs a synthetic egress test (from a test pod attempt to reach a blocked host). That gives a pass/fail attestation.

lucas: Incident response note: if the egress-detector fires (pod hits non-allowlist), auto-isolate the pod (NetworkPolicy annotate + taint node) and collect evidence: tcpdump (pcap-lite), conn metadata, and signed audit tail. Also rotate ephemeral wrapping keys and revoke tokens used by the offending pod.

kevin: Ops-bot integration: can we auto-create a certifiable report at end of canary that contains the artifact list, key fingerprints, and pass/fail checks? If yes, include a permalink in the tenant runbook.

audit-bot: Created report RPT-2026-778 (canary: canary-3) - stored in immutable-bucket://evidence/rpt-2026-778.zip - signature id: sig-0a1b2c.

maya: Nice. One more vulnerability item: keystore-connector v0.9.2 has an exposed admin endpoint. Block until v0.9.5 which drops that endpoint. Add image-gate to CVE scan and manifest preflight.

lucas: Rollout checklist for tonight: [image-scan SBOM, deploy kms-gateway, deploy provisioner-limited binding in canary ns, apply netpol to canary ns, enable audit-signer (ephemeral wrap key), run verifier, collect artifact bundle, publish report]. Canary window 23:00 UTC.

kevin: I'll schedule and tag sec-oncall. Please +1 if you can join.
maya: +1, will monitor verifier and signatures.
lucas: +1, will watch nets and run the synthetic egress tests.

kevin: Thanks - I'll update the private-deploy runbook with the artifact manifest, verifier commands, and the rollback steps (unbind role, remove netpol, revert connector image, revoke ephemeral keys).
